messages:
Erin: dropping this week's LoadWave (Nimbus) account snapshot. Quick TL;DR: WoW tokens +22%, QoQ +44%. Billing +13% WoW. p95 latency +38ms. Error rate ~5.1% (mostly 429 throttles, a few 503s during embed bursts).
Vik: thanks Erin. Is the token pressure concentrated by route or api_key?
Erin: concentrated: /v1/generate = ~60% tokens, /v1/embeddings = ~21%, /v1/rerank = ~12%. Two keys own ~82% traffic: lw-main and lw-embed. Burst windows around 10:00-10:30 UTC yesterday.
ops-bot: [ALERT] acct_loadwave - 5m 429 rate = 5.4% (threshold 3.5%). Dash: https://dd.example.com/d/loadwave/health
Maya: traces show KV-cache hit rate dropping during parallel short streams. Also embedding calls have longer seq-len and correlate with several 503s from serve-node-4 (OOM).
Julian: did they ship a product change? QoQ +44% usually means a feature.
Erin: yep, they launched an "instant-index" feature that increases embedding frequency and sends longer documents. They also rolled some traffic to rdx-3-small 3 weeks ago.
Vik: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) client-side concurrency cap (recommend 3), 2) enable prefix caching on /v1/generate, 3) route heavy embedding batches to a dedicated embed pool or async batch path, 4) soft throttle lw-embed during peak windows.
Maya: adding the query I used to slice tokens by route/key so we can paste to the AE:
```sql
SELECT api_key, route, SUM(tokens) tokens, COUNT(*) calls, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_ms,100)[OFFSET(95)] p95_ms
FROM `redwood.telemetry.events`
WHERE account_id='acct_loadwave' AND event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
GROUP BY api_key, route
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Maya: top rows: lw-main /v1/generate = 60% tokens (p95 420ms), lw-embed /v1/embeddings = 21% tokens (p95 540ms), rerank 12%.
Julian: ops notes: serve-node-4 hit OOMs during embedding bursts. We should either move embedding traffic to nodes with larger GPU mem or queue/async them. Short-term: ops can provision a dedicated embed pool with larger instances.
Erin: sample SDK guidance to share with their engineers (JS + Python):
```js
// JS: reduce concurrency and enable batching
const client = new RedwoodClient({concurrency:3, batchWindowMs:40});
client.enablePrefixCache('/v1/generate');
```
```py
# Python: prefer async batch for long-doc embeddings
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(concurrency=2, batch_window_ms=100)
# use /v1/embeddings/batch_async for long docs
```
Vik: cost modeling for AE: Option A) Provision dedicated embed pool (reduces 503s, better p95) -> +12% monthly infra cost but improves reliability. Option B) Keep current infra + enforce batching/caching + soft throttles -> -9% monthly spend but requires client changes and may still see occasional OOMs. I'll run exact numbers once Maya posts the per-route hour heatmap.
Maya: attaching a heatmap and a small chart to ticket RED-4321 (will paste links).
CSM-Amy: I'll propose a 30m enablement session focused on batching, prefix-cache, and async embeddings. Proposed slots: Thu 15:00 UTC or Fri 09:00 UTC. Amy: which works for our engineers?
Erin: propose Thu 15:00 UTC and include AE + infra. Maya: I'll bring traces and heatmap. Vik: I'll bring cost scenarios and a short ops playbook for the embed pool. Julian: I'll prepare a temporary soft-throttle config to apply if error rate >6% before the session.
CSM-Amy: noted. Action items: Maya -> post telemetry + heatmap to RED-4321; Vik -> cost scenarios; Julian -> soft-throttle PR; Erin -> schedule enablement and update AE. Reopen thread if error rate breaches 6% before Thu. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
